reconcile.note: Gill locates the Ammonite land Gad settled as Amorite territory Sihon had taken from Ammon, so Israel's conquest never touched land Deuteronomy 2:19 protects.

discrepancy.note: Colenso reads Jeremiah's rebuke of Ammon for inheriting Gad, and its threat that Israel shall repossess Ammon, as jarring with Deuteronomy's ban on taking Ammonite land.

quotes.text: With respect to the Ammonites also we read in Jer.xlix.1,4 … Concerning the Ammonites, thus saith Jehovah … hath he no heir? Why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Part I (1862), on Deuteronomy 2:19 and Jeremiah 49.

sides.snippet: and when you come near over against the children of Ammon, don't bother them, nor contend with them; for I will not give you of the land of the children of Ammon for a possession
sides.verseText: and when you come near over against the children of Ammon, don't bother them, nor contend with them; for I will not give you of the land of the children of Ammon for a possession; because I have given it to the children of Lot for a possession.

sides.snippet: it shall become a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire
sides.verseText: Therefore, behold, the days come, says Yahweh, that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard against Rabbah of the children of Ammon; and it shall become a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel possess those who did possess him, says Yahweh.
